content.title: Los Angeles Angels vs Houston Astros Live Stream: How to Watch MLB
content.text: With Mike Trout off to a hot start, the Los Angeles Angels look for a 3rd straight win over the Houston Astros on Saturday night Mike Trout, with home runs in each of the first two games of the season, leads the Los Angeles Angels (2-0) into Saturday night’s matchup with the Houston Astros (0-2) at Daikin Park in Houston. Trout, off to a 4-for-6 start, returned to center field this season after spending most of his time as the designated hitter and in right field for Los Angeles last season, playing in 130 games — the most he’s appeared in since 2019 — while slashing just .232/.359/.439 with 26 home runs. Meanwhile, the Astros got All-Star shortstop Jeremy Peña back in the lineup on Friday night after he broke a finger preparing to play for the Dominican Republic in the World Baseball Classic. How to Watch Angels vs Astros in MLB Today: Game Date: Saturday, March 28, 2026 Game Time: 7 p.m. ET TV: FanDuel Sports Network West – SW Los Angeles 3, Space City Home Network, MLB.TV – Los Angeles Angels, MLB.TV – Los Angeles Angels (Canada) Location: Daikin Park Live stream the Angels vs Astros MLB game on Fubo: Start watching now! Josh Lowe put the Angels up 4-1 with a three-run homer in the top of the second inning on Friday night while Trout went deep in the fifth and Zach Neto provided a solo shot in the ninth. Four Los Angeles relievers worked 4.1 no-hit innings after starter Yusei Kikuchi was pulled in the fifth after allowing two runs on eight hits and throwing 86 pitches. Ryan Zeferjahn earned the win with two perfect innings, working the sixth and seventh frames. Yordan Alvarez, who lost a home run on opening night when his high blast deflected off a rafter near the roof, and Peña got Houston on the board in the bottom of the first, scoring on a wild pitch and a throwing error by Angels catcher Logan O’Hoppe. Peña went 2-for-5 in his first game of the season while newcomer Mike Burrows allowed five runs on nine hits with six strikeouts in 5.2 innings. Right-hander Cristian Javier gets the start on Saturday night for the Astros. He returned from Tommy John surgery late last season and posted a 4.62 ERA and 1.270 WHIP in eight starts and 37 innings. Left-hander Reid Detmers returns to the starting rotation for Los Angeles this season after working exclusively in relief in 2025, pitching to a 3.96 ERA and 1.304 WHIP in 61 appearances and 63.2 innings with 80 strikeouts.
